title: Stripe introduces Link, a digital wallet that autonomous AI agents can use
description: Stripe has introduced Link, a new digital wallet designed to work with autonomous AI agents. This represents a significant step in enabling AI agents to perform financial transactions autonomously, bridging the gap between AI automation and commerce.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Google's Gemini AI assistant is hitting the road in millions of vehicles
description: Google is integrating its Gemini AI assistant into millions of vehicles, marking a major expansion of AI into automotive interfaces and bringing advanced conversational AI to drivers.
author: Lauren Forristal

title: Zed 1.0 Released
description: The Zed code editor has reached version 1.0. The editor, written in Rust, promises high performance and modern features for developers. The release has garnered significant attention on Hacker News with over 1900 upvotes.
author: Zed Team

title: OpenAI announces new advanced security for ChatGPT accounts, including Yubico partnership
description: OpenAI has announced enhanced security measures for ChatGPT accounts, including a partnership with Yubico for hardware security keys. This marks a significant investment in account security as AI tools become more critical to users' workflows.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: Microsoft says it has over 20M paid Copilot users
description: Microsoft has revealed that it now has over 20 million paid Copilot users, with data showing that these users are actively engaging with the AI coding assistant. This demonstrates strong adoption and usage patterns for AI coding tools.
author: Julie Bort

title: The Zig project's rationale for their anti-AI contribution policy
description: Simon Willison discusses the Zig programming language's policy against AI-generated contributions. The post explores the reasoning behind this policy and its implications for open source projects in the AI era.
author: Simon Willison

title: Copy Fail - Understanding AI Limitations
description: A viral discussion about AI failures and limitations in code generation, highlighting the importance of understanding when AI tools fail and why human oversight remains critical.
author: Community

title: Cursor Camp - Learning AI-Powered Development
description: An interactive learning platform for AI-powered development with Cursor, the AI code editor. The platform has gained significant attention with nearly 1000 upvotes on Hacker News.
author: Neal

title: OpenAI's Claude Code quality issues postmortem
description: Simon Willison analyzes Anthropic's postmortem on Claude Code quality issues. Key findings include a bug where clearing thinking from idle sessions kept happening every turn instead of once, causing forgetful behavior. Important lessons for agentic system builders about harness-level bugs.
author: Simon Willison

title: DeepSeek V4—almost on the frontier, a fraction of the price
description: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek released V4-Pro and V4-Flash preview models. Simon Willison provides analysis of their performance and pricing positioning relative to frontier models, highlighting DeepSeek's competitive positioning in the AI model landscape.
author: Simon Willison

title: Serving the For You feed - Bluesky's architecture
description: Deep dive into how spacecowboy's Bluesky feed serves 72,000 users from a single Go process with SQLite on a gaming PC (16 cores, 96GB RAM, 4TB NVMe). Total cost: $30/month. Stores 90 days of data in 419GB SQLite database. A fascinating example of efficient architecture.
author: Simon Willison

title: honker: Postgres NOTIFY/LISTEN semantics for SQLite
description: Rust SQLite extension implementing Postgres-style queue and stream functionality with transactional outbox pattern. Enables Kafka-style durable streams and queue operations in SQLite. An important addition to SQLite's capabilities for modern application patterns.
author: Simon Willison

title: Extract PDF text in your browser with LiteParse for the web
description: Simon ported LlamaIndex's LiteParse PDF extraction tool to run entirely in the browser using the same libraries as the Node.js version. Enables client-side PDF parsing without server-side processing.
author: Simon Willison

title: GPT-5.5 pelican generation via Codex backdoor API
description: Testing GPT-5.5's image generation capabilities with the classic 'pelican riding a bicycle' prompt. Found it to be fast, effective and highly capable, demonstrating OpenAI's continued progress in multimodal AI capabilities.
author: Simon Willison

title: State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
description: Lex Fridman Podcast #490 with Nathan Lambert & Sebastian Raschka discussing the current state of AI in 2026. Topics include technical breakthroughs, scaling laws, LLMs (closed and open source), programming tooling, AI agents, GPU technology, China's role in AI, and AGI progress.
author: Nathan Lambert & Sebastian Raschka

title: The people do not yearn for automation
description: Nilay Patel's written and video essay explores why AI is unpopular with the general public despite ChatGPT's skyrocketing usage. Discusses 'software brain' mindset and how people who see everything as automatable are becoming detached from the broader public who don't see coding opportunities as opportunities at all.
author: Nilay Patel

title: Colby Adcock's Scout AI raises $100M to train its models for war
description: In-depth look at Scout AI's $100M raise and their bootcamp for training AI models for military applications. The article visits their training facility and explores the intersection of AI and defense technology.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Legal AI startup Legora hits $5.6B valuation
description: Legal AI startup Legora has reached a $5.6B valuation as its battle with Harvey heats up. The legal AI space continues to see significant investment and competition as AI transforms legal workflows.
author: Anna Heim

title: Parallel Web Systems hits $2B valuation five months after its last big raise
description: Parallel Web Systems has reached a $2B valuation just five months after its previous major funding round, led by former Twitter CEO Parag Agrawal. The company's rapid valuation increase reflects strong investor interest in their technology.
author: Julie Bort

title: Meta's business AI now facilitates 10 million conversations a week
description: Meta has announced that its business AI tools are now facilitating 10 million conversations per week, showing significant adoption of AI for business messaging and customer interactions on Meta's platforms.
author: Ivan Mehta

title: Anthropic could raise a new $50B round at a valuation of $900B
description: Sources indicate that Anthropic is in discussions to raise a new $50B funding round at a $900B valuation, which would be one of the largest AI funding rounds to date and solidify Anthropic's position as a leading AI company.
author: Marina Temkin & Jagmeet Singh

title: Google Cloud surpasses $20B, but says growth was capacity-constrained
description: Google Cloud has surpassed $20B in revenue, but company officials stated that growth was constrained by capacity limitations, highlighting the infrastructure challenges in the AI boom era.
author: Sarah Perez

title: X announces a rebuilt ad platform powered by AI
description: X (formerly Twitter) has announced a completely rebuilt advertising platform powered by AI, as the company continues to leverage artificial intelligence to improve its advertising technology and revenue.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Amazon's cloud business is surging — and so is its capital spending
description: Amazon's cloud business (AWS) is experiencing significant growth, accompanied by increased capital spending as the company invests heavily in infrastructure to meet AI demand. Andy Jassy comments on the company's AI strategy.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: Meet Shapes, the app bringing humans and AI into the same group chats
description: Shapes is a new app that enables humans and AI agents to participate together in group chats, representing a novel approach to human-AI collaboration in communication platforms.
author: Aisha Malik

title: The Changelog: AI agents in software development
description: Multiple episodes of The Changelog podcast discussing AI agents in software development, including interviews with Burke Holland on GitHub Copilot and AI agents, Steve Ruiz on tldraw and AI, and Paul Dix on adapting InfluxDB to an agentic world.
author: Adam & Jerod

title: Granite 4.1: IBM's 8B Model Matching 32B MoE
description: IBM has released Granite 4.1, an 8B parameter model that reportedly matches the performance of 32B mixture-of-experts models. The release showcases IBM's continued investment in efficient AI models.
author: IBM Team

title: Alignment whack-a-mole: Finetuning activates recall of copyrighted books in LLMs
description: Research paper demonstrating how finetuning LLMs can activate recall of copyrighted books, presenting challenges for AI alignment and copyright compliance. The research highlights the complexity of preventing copyrighted content recall in AI models.
author: Researchers

title: Mike: open-source legal AI
description: Mike is an open-source legal AI tool that has gained attention on Hacker News. The project aims to provide legal AI capabilities while maintaining open-source principles.
author: Mike Team

title: DataCenter.FM – background noise app featuring the sound of the AI bubble
description: A satirical web app that plays background noise reminiscent of data centers, commenting on the AI bubble. The project has gained attention for its commentary on AI industry trends.
author: Louis Barclay

title: Firestorm Labs raises $82M to take drone factories into the field
description: Firestorm Labs has raised $82M to build drone factories inside shipping containers, bringing automated drone manufacturing closer to deployment locations. The company is pioneering field-based manufacturing capabilities.
author: Kate Park

title: Google Photos uses AI to make the iconic closet from 'Clueless' a reality
description: Google Photos has introduced AI-powered features that can organize and visualize clothing collections, reminiscent of the iconic closet from the movie 'Clueless'. The feature demonstrates AI applications in personal organization.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Mozilla's Opposition to Chrome's Prompt API
description: Mozilla has raised concerns about Chrome's Prompt API, highlighting tensions in browser AI integration standards. The discussion on GitHub explores technical and policy implications of AI prompt APIs in browsers.
author: Mozilla

title: The Biggest AI Trends and Tools Emerging in April 2026
description: AI is evolving beyond chatbots into autonomous execution systems. Key trends include coding agents becoming full software engineers, TurboQuant KV cache compression achieving 6x memory reduction, multi-agent systems replacing linear workflows, and AI runtime layers emerging as new infrastructure category.
author: Vishal Mysore

title: Noctua releases official 3D CAD models for its cooling fans
description: Noctua has released official 3D CAD models for its cooling fans, enabling better integration and customization for PC builders and case manufacturers. The release has been well-received by the community.
author: Noctua
